articleBlocks: Tortoise, Sloth, and Snail make the board look like it might just be about famously slow animals. The opening clues stay ambiguous until Traffic jams gives the board a cleaner test, so this guide starts with the misleading first read, then uses the later clues to show why the final connection is narrower than the early guesses and how each clue checks that same pattern without relying on the answer reveal too early.
Molasses supports the same idea, but it also nudges the set toward a broader theme of sluggishness.
Traffic jams are the clue that fully opens it up.
Once traffic jams join the board, the category stops being about creatures and becomes the wider idea of Slow things.
This is a simple board, but the last clue matters because it proves the theme is about pace, not species.
fullAnalysis: Tortoise, Sloth, and Snail all point toward slowness immediately, but they can also make the board look narrower than it really is.
Molasses helps by bringing in an idiomatic non-animal example, though the category can still feel like a bundle of stereotypes.
Traffic jams are the turning clue because they make it clear that the board is about slow pace in general, not just living things.
After that, each clue reads as a different example of slowness rather than as a small animal-themed cluster.
The board is straightforward, but it is well balanced because it moves from creatures to substances to everyday situations.
solutionNarrative: The animal clues made the board feel almost too obvious, which actually made it easier to overfit to creatures rather than to pace. Molasses helped widen the board, but not enough to fully break that read.
Traffic jams did the real work. Once a commuting problem joined the set, the answer became about slowness itself, and the earlier clues all fit more naturally.

lessons.title: Look for the clue that broadens the board
lessons.body: When several clues live in one obvious subgroup, the category is often wider than that subgroup appears to be.

lessons.title: Idioms can prepare a simple category
lessons.body: Molasses matters because the slow as molasses expression primes the right pace-based read before the broadening clue arrives.

lessons.title: Straightforward boards still have a pivot
lessons.body: Even easy categories often rely on one clue to prove the theme is conceptual rather than just visual or biological.
